title: Beirut Stock Exchange reported founded under the Mandate
why: Oldest Arab bourse by some accounts; reopened in 1996 after the war. Date from memory.

title: Banque de Syrie et du Grand Liban issues the Syro-Lebanese pound
why: Note issue tied to the French franc set the currency base until the 1948 split. From memory, year unconfirmed. Page: name changed to Banque de Syrie et du Grand-Liban in 1924, separate Greater Lebanon notes 1924-25; Lebanese pound formally separate from Syrian pound in 1939, peg ended 1948.
actors: Banque de Syrie et du Liban

title: Lebanon joins the IMF and World Bank
why: First external anchors of the independent state; Lebanon has had IMF Article IV rounds since. Date from memory.

title: Tapline oil terminal opens at Sidon
why: Saudi crude pipeline gave Lebanon transit fees and Sidon port traffic until the 1980s. Year from memory.

title: Intra Bank founded by Yousef Beidas
why: Became the largest Lebanese bank and the hub of Arab capital before its 1966 collapse.

title: Beirut international airport opens at Khalde
why: New airport underpinned the 1950s tourism and banking boom. Year from memory.

title: Casino du Liban opens at Maameltein
why: Flagship of Lebanon's 1960s tourism boom; later controlled through Intra Investment Company and BDL. Year from memory.

title: Middle East Airlines merges with Air Liban
why: Created the national carrier later bought by the central bank in 1996.

title: Deposit guarantee institution created after Intra collapse
why: Post-Intra rules tightened bank regulation and created a deposit guarantee body. Year from memory. Page: National Institute for the Guarantee of Deposits set up after 1966 collapse; year 1967 not stated on page.

title: Israeli raid destroys 13 MEA aircraft at Beirut airport
why: Wiped out most of the national carrier's fleet; shows early exposure of Lebanese commerce to regional conflict. Details from memory.

title: Intra Investment Company formed from Intra's good assets
why: Holding company inherited Casino du Liban, MEA and port stakes; BDL later became its dominant shareholder. Page: Intra Investment Company established 1970; BDL 35% largest holder; Casino du Liban 52%.

title: Council for Development and Reconstruction set up
why: CDR became the main channel for donor loans and postwar reconstruction contracts. Year from memory.

title: Lira breaks through 100 per dollar
why: Start of the 1987 slide to about 500 per dollar, the first lira collapse.

title: Riad Salameh becomes BDL governor
why: Ran the central bank for 30 years; peg, financial engineering and its collapse all fall in his tenure.

title: Lebanon issues its first Eurobond
why: First Arab state to borrow on Eurobond markets; the start of the dollar debt that defaulted in 2020. UPI 14 Oct 1994: $400m Eurobond, first by an Arab country.

title: Beirut Stock Exchange reopens after the war
why: Wikipedia economy page fetched: bourse reopened 1996; Israel's April 1996 operation stunted activity.

title: BDL takes 99.3% of Middle East Airlines
why: Central bank covered about $375m of MEA losses for the stake, an early case of the BDL acting as state holding. BDL acquired about 99% of MEA in 1996/97, covering $375m of losses.

title: Solidere's rebuilt Beirut Central District opens to the public
why: Downtown reconstruction became the symbol and the critique of postwar Hariri-era development. Year from search summary. Search summary says downtown opened 1999; page itself not readable (403).

title: Government cuts customs duties and adopts export promotion
why: Wikipedia economy page fetched; liberalising step before Paris II and the WTO accession bid.

title: Paris I donor conference
why: France gave EUR 500m in exchange for tax and economy modernisation commitments. Paris I held 23 Feb 2001; about EUR 500m.

title: Value-added tax takes effect
why: Wikipedia economy page fetched. VAT became a pillar of revenue; rate was 10% from launch (rate from memory).

title: EU-Lebanon Association Agreement signed
why: Set a free-trade path with the EU; entered into force in 2006 (both dates from memory).

title: State takes over cellular networks; Alfa and MTC Touch emerge
why: Two state-owned, privately managed operators became a third of state revenue by the 2010s. Year and sequence from memory. Zain got Touch management contract June 2004 (MIC2 set up 2004); MIC1/Alfa state custody began 2002, Orascom managed Alfa from 2009.

title: Stockholm donor conference after the July war
why: Pledges for war recovery came before Paris III in January 2007. Date from memory. Stockholm conference convened by Sweden 31 Aug 2006.

title: Beirut Souks open in Solidere downtown
why: 100,000 sq m retail centre rebuilt on the Roman-Greek grid; opened 2009 per search summary.

title: Offshore Petroleum Resources Law passed
why: Framework for gas licensing that led to the 2017-18 bidding round and 2026 Block 8 deal. Date and number from memory. Law No. 132 issued 24 Aug 2010.

title: Tourism hits record year before the Syria war
why: Ministry of Tourism arrivals peak in 2010; war and Gulf travel bans cut them afterwards. Figure not verified.

title: Zaitunay Bay marina and promenade opens in Solidere
why: Yacht-marina development criticised for being built over Phoenician ruins; opened 2012 per search summary.

title: Start of 27 Eurobond transactions, 2016 to 2018
why: Search summary: $12.3bn raised across 27 deals to 17 May 2018, with maturities from March 2020 to 2037; part funded BDL swaps.

title: Triple-tranche Eurobond of $3bn issued
why: $1.25bn 6.85% 2027, $1bn 7% 2032 and $0.75bn 7.25% 2037 notes, per the Ministry of Finance report.

title: Salary scale and new taxes passed together
why: Public-sector pay rise funded by tax hikes; later blamed for 2019 deficit and protest anger. Date and numbers from memory. (corrected from 2017-07-21: salary scale ratified 18 July, tax increases 19 July 2017)

title: 2017 budget passed, the first since 2005
why: Ended twelve years of spending without an approved budget. Date from memory. Parliament passed first budget since 2005 (61-4-8); source published 20 Oct 2017 gives vote date as 17 Oct, exact day unconfirmed (corrected from 2017-10-19)

title: Debt replacement deal: $1.7bn Eurobonds swapped with BDL
why: MoF issued $700m 2028 and $1bn 2031 notes to BDL in a FX/LBP replacement agreement, a financial engineering step.

title: Total, Eni and Novatek sign exploration agreements for offshore Blocks 4 and 9
why: First offshore gas licences; block 4 drilled dry in 2020. Date from memory. Cabinet approved licences Dec 2017; agreements signed 9 Feb 2018 (corrected from 'Cabinet awards')

title: Last of the 27 Eurobond deals in the 2016-18 series
why: Closes the issue spree that put $12.3bn of dollar debt with banks and BDL before default.

title: 2019 budget approved with deficit cut pledge
why: Austerity budget passed months before the October protests. Date and deficit target from memory.

title: Fitch cuts Lebanon two notches to CCC
why: Search summary: August 2019 downgrade as remittances fell; S&P held B- that month.

title: BDL starts guaranteeing dollars for fuel, wheat and medicine imports
why: Subsidy scheme at 1,515 per dollar later cost about $6bn a year and drained reserves. Timing from memory. Subsidies instituted Sept 2019 at 1,515 LBP/USD; about $6bn a year.

title: S&P cuts Lebanon to CCC/C
why: Search summary: November 2019 downgrade from B-/B, the second agency to move into deep junk.

title: Moody's cuts Lebanon to Ca; Lazard hired for the recovery plan
why: Search summaries: Moody's Ca and Lazard appointed in February 2020, with Cleary Gottlieb as legal adviser. Moody's cut to Ca on 21 Feb 2020; cabinet approved Lazard and Cleary Gottlieb on 25 Feb 2020.

title: First offshore exploration well in Block 4 comes up dry
why: Dashed early gas hopes; a second dry well followed in Block 9 in 2023. Date from memory. Drilling of Byblos well in Block 4 began 27 Feb 2020; dry result announced later in 2020 (corrected from 2020-02-27)

title: Fitch declares RD and S&P SD on Lebanon
why: Search summary: both agencies mark Lebanon in default after the March 2020 Eurobond non-payment. S&P SD on 11 Mar 2020; Fitch RD on 18 Mar 2020.

title: BDL Circular 151 lets depositors withdraw dollars in liras at 3,900
why: Search summary: launched 2020, rate later 8,000; first deposit-access circular. Exact day from memory.

title: Cabinet adopts Diab government financial recovery plan
why: Lazard-backed plan put losses near $69bn and proposed bank and BDL haircuts; banks and parliament resisted it. Date from memory.

title: IMF talks with Lebanon open, then stall over loss figures
why: Search summary: banking lobby derailed the plan and the IMF paused by spring-summer 2020. Day from memory.

title: Moody's cuts Lebanon to C
why: Search summary: July 2020 cut suggested major bondholder losses.

title: First post-blast Paris aid conference
why: Emergency humanitarian pledges channelled outside state budgets. Date and format from memory.

title: BDL Circular 154 orders banks to raise capital
why: Asked banks to inject 20% of capital in fresh dollars; partly complied, never enforced in full. Date and terms from memory.

title: Alvarez and Marsal hired for BDL forensic audit
why: Contract signed Sept 2020 per search summary; firm quit in Nov 2021 over missing data (cancellation date from memory).

title: Second Paris aid conference for Lebanon
why: Follow-up to the August 2020 meeting; aid tied to reform conditions. Date from memory.

title: Market rate reaches about 14,000 per dollar; food subsidies cut
why: Liquidity-crisis page fetched for the rate; Al Arabiya (snippet) for the food subsidy cut of 17 March. Food subsidy cut 17 Mar 2021 confirmed; reports put black-market rate between 13,000 and 15,000.

title: World Bank approves $246m emergency package
why: Wikipedia economy page fetched: emergency assistance approved March 2021.

title: BDL announces the Sayrafa exchange platform
why: Search summary: launched 10 May 2021 to record lira FX trades; initial rate set at 12,000, then rising to 38,000 in 2023.

title: BDL Circular 158 creates lollar withdrawals
why: Search summary: 300 or 400 fresh dollars monthly; raised to $500 from 1 Mar 2025.

title: Market rate hits 15,200 per dollar
why: Liquidity-crisis page fetched: June 2021 peak before Sayrafa stabilised the rate.

title: Fuel subsidies reduced under caretaker government
why: Al Jazeera: officials lifted part of fuel subsidy in late June 2021; full removal came October 2022.

title: Market rate near 24,000 per dollar
why: Evidence file (Wikipedia via search): roughly 24,000 in July 2021.

title: Government lifts price subsidies on most medicines
why: Amnesty: decision announced 9 November as BDL ran out of dollars; shortages worsened.

title: BDL Circular 161 allows dollar cash at the Sayrafa rate
why: Search summary: adopted December 2021; became a long-running partial withdrawal route.

title: Sayrafa rate becomes the rate for card payments
why: Search summary (Wikipedia lira page): from 1 Feb 2022, one of several parallel official and semi-official rates.

title: CMA CGM wins Beirut port container terminal contract
why: Al Jazeera 17 Feb 2022: ten-year operating contract from March 2022 with a $33m modernisation plan.

title: Cabinet approves electricity sector recovery plan
why: Search summary: plan approved 16 March 2022; preceded the tariff reform and IMF staff-level deal.

title: Parliament passes the 2022 budget
why: Budget on Sayrafa-linked rates; one of the IMF prior actions. Date from memory.

title: Last petrol subsidy lifted
why: Search summary: complete lifting in October 2022; by January 2023 wheat and some medicine subsidies ended too. The National, 12 Sep 2022: remaining petrol subsidy lifted (corrected from 2022-10)

title: Lebanon and Israel sign maritime boundary arrangement
why: Cleared the way for the Qana prospect and the 2026 Block 8 licences. Date from memory. Signed 27 Oct 2022 at UNIFIL Naqoura.

title: New EDL tariff takes effect: 27 cents per kWh above 100 kWh
why: The National: first EDL price rise since the 1990s, approved in August; tied to Sayrafa rate.

title: Telecom revenues fall from $1.4bn (2018) to $75m
why: Search summary: combined Alfa and Touch receipts collapsed with the lira; telecom had been a third of state revenue. SMEX 23 May 2022: combined Alfa and Touch revenues fell from $1.4bn (2018) to $75m (2022).

title: Pound hits record low of about 111,000 per dollar
why: Evidence file: record low 18 March 2023, sourced to Wikipedia via search.

title: BDL Circular 165 starts fresh-funds clearing
why: Search summary: April 2023 implementation of check and cash-transfer clearing with fresh dollars.

title: Alvarez and Marsal audit of BDL is published
why: The National: audit criticised BDL management; search summary: reserves surplus $7.2bn in 2015 became losses above $50bn by 2020.

title: BDL moves to drop the Sayrafa platform
why: AGBI Sep 2023: platform to be ditched after WB called it weak and inefficient.

title: Tourist arrivals near 1.67m before the 2024 war
why: Search summary: 1,666,492 arrivals in 2023 per Ministry of Tourism figures cited by L'Orient Today.

title: BDL official rate set at 89,500 per dollar
why: Evidence file: BDL balance sheet shows 89,500 from 31 Jan 2024; rate stayed flat through 2026. Date is 📣 (L'Orient says regime change, month unverified).

title: BDL Circular 166 takes effect
why: Search summary: $150 monthly (cap $4,350) for accounts opened 31 Oct 2019 to 30 Jun 2023; raised to $250 from March 2025.

title: Riad Salameh arrested over alleged embezzlement
why: France 24: ex-governor detained after questioning; charged with money-laundering, embezzlement, illicit enrichment.

title: World Bank: 2024 GDP cut 6.6% by the war
why: World Bank press release: cumulative real decline since 2019 above 38% by end 2024.

title: Tourist arrivals fall 32% to about 1.13m
why: L'Orient Today: 1,131,100 in 2024 against 1,666,492 in 2023; war on the southern border.

title: IMF fact-finding mission to Beirut; new programme requested
why: IMF press release: mission 10-13 March 2025; authorities asked for a new IMF-supported programme.

title: Circular 158 limit rises to $500, Circular 166 to $250
why: Search summary: monthly fresh-dollar caps raised from 1 March 2025. Raised from 1 Mar 2025.

title: IMF mission ends: bank restructuring and 2026 budget in focus
why: IMF press release: mission 28 May to 5 June 2025 started talks on a programme.

title: World Bank Spring 2025 monitor: fragile stabilisation
why: Search summary: stabilisation and tourism rebound supported 2025 growth after war.

title: Bank resolution law is Law 23 of 2025
why: Law number from search summary; TIMEP says it missed accountability chances. Same event as the parliament vote.

title: Riad Salameh freed on record bail
why: Al-Monitor: release on bail in September 2025 while cases continue.

title: Tourist arrivals rebound about 45% to 1.63m
why: Search summary of Ministry of Tourism data; 2026 war put the rebound at risk.

title: World Bank approves $350m for social protection and digital services
why: Wikipedia economy page fetched: January 2026 approval.

title: World Bank says 2025 growth was 3.5%
why: Press release: rebound with tourism and reforms; Aug 2026 monitor later revised 2025 to +4.2% (evidence file).

title: Riad Salameh arrested again
why: The National headline dated 1 Aug 2026; grounds not verified.

title: CMA CGM breaks ground on $100m Beirut terminal expansion
why: WorldCargo News: footprint 45 to 80 ha, capacity to 2.8m TEU by 2028, about 18 months of works.
